title: Duke's hands-off management and never firing anyone
summary: Duke gave men freedom, never bothered anyone and fired no one, even when Paul Gonsalves or Willie could have been.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah. Of course it was, yeah. Did you -- did you hit it off with Duke right from the start?
Yeah.
You did. You understood each other.

Yeah. Well, he never bothered a man. You would come in there, and you would just go to work. And that's all. He never said nothing to you, never speak to you. 'Hey', he'd say. That's all. Never bothered nobody.
Well, do you think that's because he liked to enjoy life, too, and that was just a good way of managing to go on enjoying life without heckling everybody and --
Well, yeah, it was a good thing, because he'd give you a lot of freedom.
Yeah.
To do anything you wanted to do.
Yeah.
You were your own boss.
Yeah. And maybe he felt that guys were entitled to that much respect, to not be pushed around.
Well, yeah. I think so. I think so.
Yeah.
You know.
Yeah. But then, on the other hand, later on, as different difficult guys came in the band --
Yeah. Then --
Well, a lot of guys caused him a lot of headaches.
Yeah.
Well, how would he do about that?
(Laughter) Sometimes he'd brush it off and ignore it. And other times he'd get a little peeved about it.
Yeah. But like you said, he never fired anybody.
No. Never fired anybody. If there was anybody to be fired it would have been Willy or been Paul Gonsalves.
(Laughter)
And he loved Paul, didn't he?
Yeah.
He really loved Paul. That was one thing

about him, to my feel. The guys -- the guys that -- well, everybody has their different favorites that were in the band, etcetera, etcetera, but the guys that you feel like were the heart of the band, they were the guys that he particularly loved, didn't he? I mean -- well, I mean, he loved you, he loved Harry, he loved Tricky Sam.
Yeah. Uh-huh.
And I mean, Tricky wasn't a guy that did much talking or anything. Did a lot of mixing with people, did he?
No. Tricky didn't do anything. People that he liked he would go around with and drink with, you know. Guys in the band that he liked, you know.

Well, remember when Tricky used to sit up there and do the shim-sham on the stand, and the band would be doing a background and -- you may not have noticed, because you were up there in the trumpets, but he used to do a thing, and he'd get all of the section doing it with him. Well, but, well, there were a lot of different guys. Harold Baker, for instance. I mean, he was a little difficult to handle at times, wasn't he?
I wasn't there during --
Oh, weren't you?
-- during his period.
Oh, I wanted to ask you about Harold. Well,
